sections.h2: Where to start a Carteret sale
sections.html:
Begin with the borough's occupancy inspection and a current tax bill. A Carteret sale can go through an agent, a for-sale-by-owner listing or an investor, and all three paths pass the same two checkpoints. After those, the deed gets filed in New Brunswick at the Middlesex County Clerk's Registry.

About 55 percent of Carteret homes are lived in by their owners, which leaves a large share of the housing stock as rentals. Sellers therefore include landlords, heirs and people with older houses and repairs put off. For those owners the paperwork below weighs as much as the listing photos, so read it before you set a closing date.

Carteret sits in northeastern Middlesex County, on the Arthur Kill across from Staten Island, and Woodbridge Township touches it on every land side. Local place names still in use include Chrome, Lamar, Canda, Silvan Beach and West Carteret, the part west of the Turnpike.

  • Residents: 25,781
  • Share of homes lived in by owners: 54.7%
  • Typical owner-occupied home value: $405,800
  • Typical gross rent: $2,032
  • Households: 8,224, averaging 3.10 people
  • Household income, midpoint: $96,862

The borough's occupancy form has separate lines for one-family and two-family houses, and a house with a clean certificate and working mechanicals gives a buyer fewer reasons to renegotiate.

Access is the strength here, though some buyers will want to talk about truck traffic. The New Jersey Turnpike is the only major highway through the borough, with Interchange 12 inside its limits. NJ Transit local buses run the 116 route toward Midtown Manhattan and Perth Amboy and the 48 route toward Elizabeth. The average commute is 31.4 minutes.

With an economy built around freight and warehousing, buyers may ask about noise, truck routes and flood exposure along the Arthur Kill and Rahway River edges. Walk the block at rush hour before you price the house so you can answer honestly.

  • Know how far the house sits from the Turnpike ramps and from CR 602.
  • Pull together any flood or sump-pump history, since tidal water borders the east side.
  • Keep the block and lot number handy, because every borough form asks for it.

Carteret requires a residential certificate of continued occupancy, issued by the Department of Code Enforcement at 61 Cooke Avenue, before a house changes hands. The application asks for the owner, the purchaser, the realtor if there is one, the block and lot, one family or two, the listed price and the names and ages of everyone living there. Code enforcement answers at (732) 541-3925, and inspections are booked through (732) 541-3810.

An addendum to the application works as a plain checklist, and the inspector holds you to it. The seller certifies each item, and the form warns that false statements can be prosecuted with a fine of $2,000 per occurrence.

  • Smoke detectors on each level, plus a smoke detector and carbon monoxide alarm outside every sleeping area, within ten feet.
  • Battery-powered units that carry sealed 10-year batteries.
  • A 2A:10BC fire extinguisher mounted near the kitchen, also within ten feet.
  • Working heat, hot water, electric, water and sewer.
  • No unpermitted work and no open permits.
  • Exterior, grounds, concrete, asphalt and masonry free of disrepair and trip hazards.
Carteret occupancy application charges
ServiceAmount or rule
Inspection, one-family house$100
Inspection, two-family house$150
Temporary certificate$75
Name change on an existing certificate$50
Added inspection after a failure or no-show$50 each
Life of the applicationVoid 90 days after issuance

The base fee pays for the first visit and one follow-up. Since the application lapses after 90 days, file it close to your expected closing rather than months ahead. Pay by cash, certified check, or an attorney or broker check. The borough reserves the right to inspect again later.

Carteret sends a single tax bill each July. Its stubs cover four installments, payable February 1, May 1, August 1 and November 1, and finance gives you ten days of grace on each. Once grace ends, interest runs from the original due date at 8 percent a year on the first $1,500 owed and 18 percent on whatever exceeds it. Owing more than $10,000 adds a 6 percent penalty at year-end, and a balance that sits unpaid for a year or longer goes into the yearly tax sale.

Bring the latest bill to the closing table, because the buyer's side needs the next installment amount. The tax collector works from the finance department at 100 Cooke Avenue on weekdays between 8 a.m. and 4 p.m. Call (732) 541-3820 extension 3818 for a payoff figure.

If you believe the assessment is off, take it up with the borough assessor first, at extension 3110. Next comes an appeal package from the Middlesex County Tax Board in New Brunswick. The state deadline is April 1, moved to May 1 in a revalued town, and the owner must show the assessed value is unreasonable next to market value. People who hold a senior or veteran deduction also send in an annual statement by March 1 to keep it.

sections.h2: Recording the deed and state tax forms
sections.html:
Your deed goes to the Middlesex County Clerk's Registry on the fourth floor at 75 Bayard Street in New Brunswick. Walk-ins are weekdays, and arriving by 4 p.m. is wise. An attorney or title company normally makes the filing. Online records reach back to 1929 for deeds and 1950 for mortgages, which lets you pull your own chain of title before listing, though the staff will not run a title search for you.

Recording costs $45 for the first page of a deed, $10 for each extra page and a $6 name fee after the fifth name. The state adds its own charges: the seller pays the realty transfer fee, and every seller submits a gross income tax form. Residents of New Jersey sign a residency certification and settle income tax on their regular return. Someone who has moved out of state, even a longtime Carteret owner, prepays either two percent of the price or 8.97 percent of the net gain, unless the form lists an exemption that fits.

If you lived in the house two of the last five years, the first $250,000 of gain is tax free under federal rules, or $500,000 for a married couple, and New Jersey follows the same approach.

sections.h2: Which route sells a Carteret house fastest?
sections.html:
The quickest routes are a cash purchase from an investor or a short listing of a well-prepared house, and the borough certificate gates both. A cash purchase removes the lender's appraisal and underwriting, yet the inspection, the tax payoff and the deed filing still apply.

  • An agent suits a house in good shape when you can tolerate showings and wait on a buyer's lender.
  • An as-is investor purchase suits a house needing work, one with tenants, back taxes or an estate behind it.
  • Choose a sale by owner only with an attorney lined up for the contract, the certificate and the closing forms.

Whichever way you go, order the inspection early, replace alarms and the extinguisher yourself, and ask the buyer's attorney who will book the final walk-through. If a repair cannot be finished before the closing date, ask the borough code office whether a temporary certificate is available.

faqs.q: Is an occupancy inspection mandatory for Carteret sellers?
faqs.a: Yes. The Department of Code Enforcement issues a residential certificate of continued occupancy after an inspection, and the application lapses 90 days after issuance, so time it close to closing.

faqs.q: How much does the Carteret inspection run?
faqs.a: It is $100 for a one-family house and $150 for a two-family house. A temporary certificate is $75, and every extra inspection after a failure or no-show is $50.

faqs.q: What are Carteret's quarterly tax dates?
faqs.a: Installments fall on the first of February, May, August and November, with ten days of grace. Late balances accrue 8 percent a year up to $1,500 and 18 percent on anything above that.

faqs.q: Which Middlesex County office files a Carteret deed?
faqs.a: The County Clerk's Registry at 75 Bayard Street in New Brunswick. A closing attorney or title agent usually delivers it with the state transfer and income tax forms.

faqs.q: Can a Carteret house with tenants or open repairs still sell?
faqs.a: Yes, but the occupancy inspection still applies and the application lists everyone living in the home. Ask the code office about open permits first, since none may be open.
